series.label: Federal net balance per resident · annual history
series.definition: Published matched fiscal balances from one 2025 publisher vintage; nominal fiscal-year values, not inflation-adjusted. Preliminary/revised status is preserved.
limitations: Detailed matched receipts/spending are FFY 2023 preliminary estimates. FY 2022 and earlier history retain the 2025 report’s revisions; no FY 2024/2025 federal balance is claimed.
The federal fiscal year is October 1 through September 30; per-capita denominators use publisher Census estimates for the associated calendar year.
DC and territories are outside the published tables for 50 states: DC stays explicitly missing in every fiscal map.
These are allocated federal-budget estimates using a mixture of actual data and proxies, sometimes prior-year allocators, not raw tax-collection-location totals.
Included spending covers direct benefits, grants, contracts, wages and COVID relief; national debt interest and other unallocable items are not all assigned to states.
Source printed monetary totals are rounded to millions, per-capita cells to dollars and ratios to 0.01; small arithmetic differences remain rather than rewriting source numbers.

Positive or negative balance is not a state-government budget surplus/deficit, an individual tax bill, an economic impact estimate or a moral ranking. Federal deficit financing means state balances need not sum to zero.
Nominal dollars are not inflation-adjusted. Do not subtract this separate Census state-tax layer from federal spending or compare different fiscal periods as one balance.
series.hosted_scope_note: All retained observations for this measure in the named built-in dataset.
